commands.tip: WordPress always has one active theme. Delete unused inactive themes — they're a security risk if outdated.
Use --status=inactive to audit unused themes. Use --format=json to pipe into scripts.

Returns exit code 0 if installed, 1 if not. Use in scripts: if ! wp theme is-installed storefront; then wp theme install storefront --activate; fi
Use wp theme mod set <key> <value> to update customizer settings from the terminal — useful in automated workflows.
Subcommands: get, set, remove. Example: wp theme mod set header_textcolor 333333
Returns slug, rating, and active installs. Use the slug with wp theme install.

commands.output:
Theme commands manage WordPress themes from the terminal.

Available commands:
• wp theme list              - List all installed themes
• wp theme install <slug>    - Install from repository or ZIP
• wp theme activate <slug>   - Switch active theme
• wp theme update --all      - Update all themes
• wp theme delete <slug>     - Remove theme files
• wp theme get <slug>        - Get theme details
• wp theme is-installed      - Check if installed
• wp theme mod get/set       - Manage customizer settings
• wp theme search <term>     - Search repository

Anchors:
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/themes/#wp-theme-list
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/themes/#wp-theme-install
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/themes/#wp-theme-activate
→ 4wp.dev/wp-cli/themes/#wp-theme-mod-get--set--remove
commands.tip: Install parent theme first, then child theme. Activate the child — not the parent.
